title: Under the Kingdom of Tondo
description: A settlement of some 800 farmers and fishermen thrives as part of the Kingdom of Tondo.

title: Encomienda del Tondo
description: The settlement is formally acknowledged as part of the Encomienda del Tondo under Spanish rule.

title: Founding of the Pueblo
description: On April 4, Taguig is established as a separate pueblo of Manila province, made up of nine barangays. Its name comes from 'taga-giik', the rice threshers the early settlers were known as.

title: Revolution in the Hills
description: On February 6, Filipino revolutionary forces dislodge an American position in the hills of Taguig during the Philippine–American War.

title: Into Rizal Province
description: Proclaimed an independent municipality in 1900, Taguig is incorporated into the newly created province of Rizal on June 11, 1901.

title: Fort William McKinley
description: The United States acquires 25.78 km² of Taguig land for Fort William McKinley, the military reservation that later becomes Fort Bonifacio.

title: Independent Again
description: After being merged with Pateros and Muntinlupa in 1903, Taguig and Pateros are separated into distinct municipalities of Rizal.

title: Fort McKinley Turned Over
description: On May 14, Fort McKinley is transferred to the Philippine government; it is later renamed Fort Bonifacio.

title: New Town Center
description: On August 1, the municipal seat moves from Santa Ana to Tuktukan, where the old city hall still stands.

title: Joining Metro Manila
description: On November 7, Presidential Decree No. 824 separates Taguig from Rizal and makes it part of the newly formed National Capital Region.

title: The Cityhood Law
description: Republic Act No. 8487 is enacted to convert Taguig into a highly urbanized city, but the April 25 plebiscite initially shows voters against it.

title: Taguig Becomes a City
description: After a Supreme Court-ordered recount of the plebiscite votes, Taguig officially becomes a city on December 8.

title: 28 Barangays
description: On December 18, ten new barangays are created, bringing Taguig's total to 28.

title: Fort Bonifacio and EMBO
description: The Supreme Court's ruling affirming Taguig's jurisdiction over Fort Bonifacio and the ten EMBO barangays becomes final, bringing the city to 38 barangays.
